laws.rule: In Nara Park, do not feed the deer anything except shika senbei (deer crackers); bread, sweets, vegetables and leftovers are banned. The deer are wild animals: do not hit or chase them, and keep bags and rubbish out of their reach.
laws.heading: Nara Prefecture, How to treat the deer in Nara Park

laws.rule: Nara Ordinance on the Healthy Development of Young People (奈良県青少年の健全育成に関する条例), art. 32. The ordinance sets the late-night period as 11 pm to 4 am. A guardian must try not to let a young person (generally under 18) go out in that period without special reason; the guardian's own duty has no penalty. Anyone else is barred from taking such a young person out, going about with them or keeping them out in that period without the guardian's consent or another proper reason. The offence for others carries a fine of up to JPY 300,000 (about A$2,707). Rates: RBA 30 Oct 2026, A$1 = JPY 110.82.

sites.name: Hōryū-ji
sites.what: Buddhist temple at Ikaruga with some of the world's oldest surviving wooden buildings (UNESCO World Heritage).

access.opening: 22 February to 3 November 8 am to 5 pm; 4 November to 21 February 8 am to 4.30 pm; last entry 30 minutes before closing.
access.tickets: Adults JPY 2,000 (about AUD 18, RBA rate 30 October 2026), junior high JPY 1,700, primary JPY 1,000; covers the western precinct, Great Treasure Hall and eastern precinct. Cash only.

culture-and-protocol.dress_and_conduct: Nara Park's deer are wild animals. Don't touch them carelessly or let children approach them alone; they may charge, butt, bite or kick, especially mothers in spring and stags in autumn. Feeding anything other than shika senbei (deer crackers) is prohibited in Nara Park. Don't leave rubbish.
culture-and-protocol.sacred_or_restricted_places: Nara Park deer are protected; treat them with care.
